question: Which bank is called 'lender of last resort' in Indian monetary system?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the lender of last resort in India's monetary system.
 
• The RBI is India's central bank and is responsible for regulating the banking system, controlling monetary policy, and issuing banknotes. 
 
• The RBI's role as the lender of last resort means that it can provide liquidity to banks that are solvent but temporarily facing liquidity issues.
 
• This can happen when no other bank is willing to extend credit to the bank in need. 
 
• The RBI was established on April 1, 1935, and was originally privately owned. It was nationalized in 1949 and is now fully owned by the Government of India.
